newsitem.title: UK: Kingfisher off on press comment, lack of bid.
newsitem.headline: Kingfisher off on press comment, lack of bid.

text.p: Shares in retailer Kingfisher Plc slipped on Monday as a rumoured bid failed to emerge and the weekend press highlighted Kingfisher as a possible frontrunner for the purchase of the Littlewoods stores.
The shares were off 14p to 672-1/2p by 0942 GMT.

"We had a good market on Friday," said one senior trader. "There were all sorts of bid rumours flying around." The shares had finished 4-1/2p higher on Friday, helped by vague rumours of a possible bid emerging for the retail group, but traders said the stock was trading lower on Monday as the rumours subsided. "We have seen no evidence of one (a bid) coming through today and the press said Kingfisher could be the frontrunner for the Littlewoods LWD.CN stores, though analysts are largely dismissing those thoughts."

"There was a rumour that the French retailer Pinault-Printemps Redoute was going to bid for Kingfisher, which was good for a few pence on Friday, but I don't think it was that credible," said industry analyst Nick Bubb at Mees Pierson. A report in the Sunday Times which said Kingfisher was a strong contender for the 500 million stg auction of 134 Littlewoods LWD.CN stores also helped to depress the shares, traders said. "I think Kingfisher would like the odd site to add to its portfolio but I'd be surprised if they went for the whole lot," Bubb said. "They are a pretty cautious company and I would take all these "frontrunner" stories with a pinch of salt." Bubb said there was no reason to believe Kingfisher's results next week would be disappointing, commenting that the share price weakness presented a good buying opportunity ahead of the figures. The analyst maintains his "buy" rating on the stock and a price target of 750p.
